reason: Reproduced exactly, on both grounds, at both sizes, from a fresh load of ?state=owner-flight. Before Add: .b-shared = 'Live since 15 July · anyone with the link can read it', [data-act=publish] = 'Get the link' (w=103, right edge 1254), Add a moment x=925, Preview x=1060, foot 'Updated 15 July 2026'. One click on Add a moment: .b-shared = 'Only you can see this', verb = 'Publish' (w=75), Add a moment x=953, Preview x=1088, foot 'Updated 16 July 2026'. Identical on ?v=ink; at 390 the bar is left-anchored so nothing shifts, but the status line and the verb flip the same way. The damage is not cosmetic and it is not confined to the bar: window.__TLCORE.F.publication goes {state:'published',publishedAt:'2026-07-15'} -> {state:'draft',publishedAt:null}, and pressing Publish afterwards lands on the draft press screen, 'Send it to Mara & Finn.', for a plan whose link is still live and still readable by everyone holding it. 'Only you can see this' is simply false at that moment. Pressing Undo restores the row (7 -> 8 -> 7) but not the record: .b-shared stays 'Only you can see this' and the verb stays 'Publish' for the rest of the session, so the product's own way out of a mistake does not reach the object it damaged. Checked every escape route for the write and none holds. (1) Not already handled. The comment at render-b.js:1245 justifies the write by the first-moment-ever case, but that case is served by a separate write at render-b.js:1615 inside the owner-empty handler, which runs before go('owner-flight'). Driven: owner-empty -> '3 October 2026' -> Set the day -> Add a moment leaves F.publication {state:'draft'} with 1 milestone, and a second Add from the bar is a no-op on an already-draft record. So line 1249 only ever CHANGES anything in the one case where the change is wrong. (2) Not a gate restatement. interaction-check.mjs:1757 asserts /live since/ on a fresh owner-flight paint and :2625 asserts the verb against FIXTURE.publication.state on first paint; the four blocks that click [data-act=add] (:866, :1286, :1475, :2834) assert row counts, ids, focus and titles and never look at .b-shared, the verb or F.publication. Removing the write regresses nothing the gate holds. (3) Not settled. SETTLED's draft-branch-restored-before-it-is-used is about state=owner-draft borrowing the record for one paint; this is the reverse write on a live plan and was not raised. Nothing in lock.md or LANGUAGE.md declares an edit-invalidates-the-share model, and the copy path at :1278 states the opposite model outright — 'Taking the link IS the publish'. (4) The proposed fix keeps the new-project case working: verified above, that path never reaches 1249. It violates no constraint, touches no colour, weight or architecture.
sharpenedFix: The guard as written is correct in effect but dead in practice, so state it as what it is. F.milestones cannot be driven to zero through the UI — past moments have no Delete, and deleting everything reachable bottoms out at 4 records with the plan still published — so `if (!F.milestones.length)` can never be true at render-b.js:1249. Delete the write instead: remove `F.publication = { state: "draft", publishedAt: null };` from the add branch entirely and rewrite the comment above it to point at render-b.js:1615, which is where a brand-new plan is actually made a draft, before go('owner-flight'). Keep the F.updatedLabel write and the paintPublication(root) call — the stamp should move, and repainting an unchanged record is a no-op. If the founder wants a guard rather than a deletion, key it to the first-run flag (the same condition owner-empty already sets), never to array length: adding a moment to a live plan and adding one to a plan that has been emptied are the same act and both must leave the publication record alone. Then three gate assertions, written first and watched fail: on state=owner-flight, click [data-act="add"] and assert .b-shared still starts 'Live since' and [data-act="publish"] still reads 'Get the link'; assert the foot stamp DID move to 16 July in the same step, so the fix cannot be over-applied; and click [data-act="publish"] afterwards and assert the press headline still reads 'Mara & Finn have had this since 15 July.' Run all three on ?v=paper and ?v=ink.
